target_customer: Gen Z and young adults (18 to 27) who want to meet people in person, plus local venues that host them
problem: Young people are lonely and dating or friend apps rely on swiping and profiles. 222 uses AI to arrange real life meetups with strangers or friends at local venues.
business_model: Consumer app with per experience fees and a subscription, plus venue partnerships

founders.name: Keyan Kazemian
education: USC or UC Irvine, per one press report (founders attended school there)
founders.background_notes: Co-launched 222 in late 2021 as a backyard dinner series in Los Angeles.

founders.name: Danial Hashemi
founders.background_notes: Describes himself as an Iranian immigrant building a new solution to social.

competitors.name: Flox
competitors.what: App helping friend groups meet other friend groups, popular with NYC college students
competitors.traction_then: Wooing college students in NYC per TechCrunch coverage
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in the source reviewed

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app with personality quiz matching and venue booking is standard consumer engineering. The hard part is operations and supply of venues and attendees, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided local liquidity of venues and users helps, but Timeleft, Bumble BFF and many dinner apps copy the format easily.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bumble BFF, Meetup and Timeleft kept expanding and similar apps multiplied through 2024 and 2025. No incumbent bought or shut down 222.

market_need_then: Loneliness among Gen Z and post pandemic desire for in person connection were widely covered. The founders ran dinner events first to test demand before building the app.

branding.name_origin: Press reports say the name comes from the street address in Los Angeles where the idea started (single secondary source).

identity.visual_style: Polaroid style photo frames in a scrapbook layout
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, playful, lowercase headlines such as let us plan

branding.brand_signature: No swiping, no profiles, no DMs: the AI picks who you meet
branding.community_and_virality: Frequent coverage in TechCrunch, LA Times, Business Insider, Fast Company and the Wall Street Journal (Dec 2025). A matcha event series and bartender anecdotes suggest a local scene, but no merch was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short number name and a clear no swiping positioning earned unusually wide press, but a numeric name is hard to search and easy to confuse.

pivots.from: In person dinner series in Los Angeles
pivots.to: Mobile app with AI matching and event invitations at local venues
pivots.why: Scale beyond hosting dinners by hand

outcome_analysis: 222 grew from backyard dinners in Los Angeles in 2021 to an app with press in TechCrunch, Business Insider and the Wall Street Journal. It raised a pre-seed in 2022 and, per aggregators, a seed and a roughly $10M Series A in December 2025, and a redesign in 2026 focused on group meetups. It remains Active with a team of 28. Success so far rests on a loneliness tailwind and strong earned media, while copycat dinner apps are the main threat.
notes: Unverified aggregator figures: seed $2.5M (1517 Fund, General Catalyst, Best Nights VC) around October 2024 and Series A $10.1M in December 2025 led by Upfront Ventures (Seedtable, VCBacked); totals vary by source ($11.6M to $16.8M). They are not recorded as rounds. Pre-seed amount comes from a TechCrunch story as syndicated by AOL, dated by search to November 2022. The YC page says founded 2023 but sources show activity from late 2021. Founders' education is from one press summary and unverified. Only one dated competitor was found near the batch.
